## Appearance

Gilbert Blythe is a tall, broad-shouldered young man with a frank face and curly brown hair. He has roguish, clear, and straightforward hazel eyes, along with a mouth often twisted into a teasing smile.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot P28](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0028), [v1 CHAPTER XXVIII. An Unfortunate Lily Maid P32](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0032), [v2 XIX Just a Happy Day P50](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0050)_

## Personality

Gilbert is a clever, ambitious, and good-natured young man who is known for his kind, thoughtful manner as well as his penchant for teasing girls. Determined to get the most out of life, he aims to pay his own way through college. He has firmly decided that his ultimate goal is to become a doctor.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot P16](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0016), [v1 CHAPTER XVII. ## History

Gilbert Blythe spent three years in Alberta with his sick father and spent a summer visiting cousins in [New Brunswick](../codex/places.md#new-brunswick) before returning home. Upon his return to school, he teased [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) by pulling her braid and calling her 'Carrots,' causing her to smash a slate over his head and angrily refuse his apology. Although [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) maintained a fierce academic rivalry with him over the following years, Gilbert rescued her when she was stranded on a bridge pile, though she again rejected his offer of friendship. Later, Gilbert won the medal at Queen's [Academy](../codex/places.md#queen-s-academy) while [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) won the Avery Scholarship. Upon learning that [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) planned to give up her scholarship to remain in [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea) with [Marilla](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md), Gilbert gave up his position as the [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea) school teacher so [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) could have it, leading [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) to finally end their feud and become close friends. As a teacher himself, Gilbert discussed teaching methods and creative pursuits with [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) and joined her in various local matters, including the [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea) Village [Improvement Society](../codex/factions.md#improvers). He remained a constant companion and friend to [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md), spending time with her in conversation after village events and shared experiences.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot P16](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0016), [v1 CHAPTER XV. ## Quotes

> "It wasn’t particularly good of me at all, Anne. I was pleased to be able to do you some small service. Are we going to be friends after this? Have you really forgiven me my old fault?"
>
> — Gilbert Blythe — [v1 CHAPTER XXXVIII. The Bend in the Road P52](../source/v01-c38.md#nw-v01-c38-p0052)

> "We were born to be good friends, Anne. You’ve thwarted destiny enough. I know we can help each other in many ways. You are going to keep up your studies, aren’t you? So am I. Come, I’m going to walk home with you."
>
> — Gilbert Blythe — [v1 CHAPTER XXXVIII. The Bend in the Road P55](../source/v01-c38.md#nw-v01-c38-p0055)

> “Not she,” said Gilbert emphatically. “I know Louisa Spencer well. She doesn’t ‘believe’ in Village Improvement Societies, but she does believe in dollars and cents. She’d be more likely to urge Judson on than to dissuade him.”
>
> — Gilbert Blythe — [v2 XIV A Danger Averted P46](../source/v02-c14.md#nw-v02-c14-p0046)

> “All right!” Gilbert sprang into his skiff with an angry color in his cheeks. “I’ll never ask you to be friends again, Anne Shirley. And I don’t care either!”
>
> — Gilbert Blythe — [v1 CHAPTER XXVIII. An Unfortunate Lily Maid P34](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0034)

> "Well, I must run up to MacPhersons’. Moody Spurgeon came home from Queen’s today for Sunday and he was to bring me out a book Professor Boyd is lending me."
>
> — Gilbert Blythe — [v2 VII The Pointing of Duty P19](../source/v02-c07.md#nw-v02-c07-p0019)

## Relationships

### [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/anne-shirley--gilbert-blythe.md)

Gilbert and [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) began as bitter enemies after he teased her on his return to school, causing [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) to hold a long-standing grudge despite his attempts to apologize and even saving her when her boat leaked. They were fierce academic rivals competing for top marks in school, but [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) eventually forgave him. By the second volume, they have become close friends who write newspaper notes together as literary collaborators, with Gilbert harboring romantic feelings for her.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot P16](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0016), [v1 CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot P33](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0033), [v1 CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot P38](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0038), +34 more_
